West Indies Secure Eight-Wicket Victory Over Bangladesh in First Test

01 Nov 2026, 06:00 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.aljazeera.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysOn Saturday, the West Indies secured an eight-wicket victory against Bangladesh in the first Test match in Mirpur, claiming a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

  1. West Indies Take 1-0 Series Lead in Mirpur
  2. Bowling Performances and Match Turning Points

West Indies Take 1-0 Series Lead in Mirpur

On Saturday, the West Indies secured an eight-wicket victory against Bangladesh in the first Test match in Mirpur, claiming a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

Chasing a target of 170 on the fourth day, the visitors reached the goal in 35.1 overs, finishing at 170 for two. Brandon King led the chase with an unbeaten 81 off 115 balls, featuring 10 fours and a six. Opening partner John Campbell contributed 49 runs from 55 balls before being bowled by Shoriful Islam.

Bowling Performances and Match Turning Points

Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings after resuming the fourth day at 79-6.

  • Jomel Warrican: Claimed 4-63 in the second innings, adding to his five-wicket haul in the first innings. He was named player of the match.
  • Roston Chase: The West Indies captain took 5-36 in the second innings, marking his fifth career five-wicket haul in Test cricket.
  • Nayeem Hasan: Provided notable resistance for Bangladesh, scoring 52 off 91 balls to record his maiden Test half-century before being caught off Chase's bowling.

Post-Match Comments

West Indies captain Roston Chase attributed the win to team resilience following a difficult start.

"The guys were determined, even though we didn’t have a good start in the first innings," Chase said after the match. "We lost the lead, but we were still determined to fight back and try to win the game, and that’s what we did."

Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto acknowledged shortcomings across all departments, particularly in the field.

"All three departments didn’t do well, especially in the field. These things can happen sometimes, but I believe the intention and preparation were quite good," Shanto stated.

Weather Delays and Upcoming Fixtures

Play was interrupted twice during the West Indies' second innings: first by rain following a 64-run opening partnership, and later by bad light and lightning, causing a 45-minute stoppage.

The second and final Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Sylhet on November 5.
